drug_class: Antisense oligonucleotide (a type of gene-targeting medicine)
purpose: Nusinersen is used to treat spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), a rare genetic condition that causes muscle weakness and makes it hard to move, breathe, and swallow. It works in both children and adults with SMA. The goal is to help improve muscle strength and function over time.
how_it_works: SMA is caused by a faulty gene that stops the body from making enough of a protein the nerves and muscles need to work properly. Nusinersen is a specially designed molecule that tells the body to produce more of that important protein. By increasing this protein, the medicine helps protect the nerve cells that control your muscles.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include lower respiratory infections (like pneumonia or bronchitis), upper respiratory infections (like a cold), constipation, and headache. Some people also experience fever, back pain, or post-lumbar puncture headache since the medicine is given by injection into the spinal fluid.
warnings: Because this medicine is injected directly into the fluid around your spine, there is a small risk of bleeding problems — your doctor will check your blood clotting before each dose. Rare but serious kidney problems have been reported, so your kidney function will be monitored regularly. Always tell your doctor about all medications you take and report any unusual bruising, bleeding, or changes in urination right away.
typical_dosing: Nusinersen is given as an injection into the fluid around your spinal cord (called an intrathecal injection) by a specialist doctor. You receive 4 loading doses over the first 2 months — on days 1, 15, 29, and 64. After that, you receive a maintenance dose once every 4 months for the rest of your life. Each dose is given in a clinic or hospital setting.
